name: Jehoshaphat
overview: Jehoshaphat was a male figure known as the son of Ahilud and served as a recorder in King David's kingdom. His role as a recorder indicates a position of administrative responsibility during David's reign. No further tribal or personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehoshaphat means 'YHWH has judged,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names that acknowledges God's sovereignty. He also held the title of 'recorder,' which denotes an official responsible for keeping records or serving as a clerk or secretary in the royal administration.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Jehoshaphat as the son of Ahilud, establishing his paternal lineage. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jehoshaphat's significance lies in his role as a recorder under King David, which placed him in a trusted position within the administration of Israel's kingdom. His name, meaning 'YHWH has judged,' aligns with the biblical emphasis on God's righteous governance. Although details about his life are limited, his service during David's reign situates him within the foundational period of Israel's monarchy, contributing to the orderly governance that God established through David's rule.

keyEvents.event: Allied with Ahab against Ramoth Gilead
